transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-03
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Javier Ortega (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Liam Park (Redwood Solutions), Samantha Lee (Horizon CTO), Marcus Hill (Horizon Lead ML Eng), Priya Patel (Horizon Eng Manager)

Summary (auto): Hosted API demo covering streaming and param controls, retries, and quick Console overview; next steps include pricing, security docs and a short pilot.

00:00 Javier: Hello everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Javier from Redwood, i'll hand over to Maya to run the demo.
00:06 Maya: Hey team -- hi Samantha, Marcus, Priya -- quick agenda: 1) hosted API basics 2) streaming and params 3) retries and SDK tips 4) Redwood Console walkthrough and metrics. If you have questions please interrupt.
00:20 Samantha: Sounds good -- our main concern is latency and cost, we want something that can run inline on checkout flows so p50 under 200ms is ideal.
00:28 Javier: Got it, that's helpful context. Marcus, curious about your current infra?
00:33 Marcus: We're on GCP, most of inference today is a mix of hosted third-party APIs and some on-prem models. Throughput right now is spiky, peaks around 300 reqs/min for conversational upsell flows.
00:45 Maya: Perfect, we'll show how Redwood's Hosted API handles batching and streaming to keep latency low while still being cost-effective.
01:00 Maya: Demo start \u0014 showing basic POST /v1/chat.completions, here's an example in Python. (screen share)
01:10 Maya: Key params: model, messages, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, and stream true|false. By default we have a conservative temperature of 0.2 for deterministic responses. You can tune per-route.
01:30 Marcus: When you say stream, does that mean token by token over a socket? Do you support SSE?
01:36 Maya: Yes, we support streaming via server-sent events and chunked HTTP responses in the SDKs. You get partial tokens as they're generated which helps perceived latency on the client. Note: streaming still counts tokens for billing as they are produced.
01:55 Samantha: Are there any gotchas for streaming and retries? If a request fails mid-stream how do we guarantee idempotency?
02:05 Maya: Good question. The Hosted API has request ids you can set (client_request_id) and idempotency tokens for non-streaming operations. For streaming we recommend a short retry/backoff and resume logic on your side; we also offer at-most-once and exactly-once semantics for certain dedicated plans but hosted default is at-least-once for best availability.
02:28 Priya: Could you repeat the plan names? I heard Dedicated gives stronger guarantees?
02:33 Javier: Right \u0014 Dedicated capacity customers can opt into stronger idempotency/fenced execution semantics since they control the pool. Hosted is optimized for broad availability and falls back to compatible model variants when needed.
02:46 Maya: Back to params: temperature affects randomness, top_p is nucleus sampling. For shorter deterministic text like product labeling we typically keep temp 0.0-0.3. For creative suggestions you might use 0.7+. max_tokens caps output length; we also show token usage in the Console so you can tune cost.
03:10 Marcus: How about tokenization differences across models? Do you standardize billing?
03:17 Maya: Billing is token-based; models differ on tokens per payload. In the Console you'll see per-model token counts and cost breakdowns. We also surface recommended quantized variants for cost-sensitive workloads.
03:30 Liam: Quick note on SDKs \u0014 our SDKs handle retries with exponential backoff and jitter; you can override retry policies per-route.
03:40 Samantha: Rate limits? We have bursts during marketing pushes, is there burst capacity?
03:46 Maya: Yes, Hosted has per-account rate limits with burst allowances. If you need predictable bursts you can buy reserved capacity (Dedicated) or configure burst pools. We'll include recommended rate limit settings based on your traffic profile.
03:58 Maya: Now I'll demo streaming: sending a multi-turn chat, stream true, you can see partial messages as they come in... (stream plays)
04:20 Marcus: I see latency to first token is low, but full response can take a few hundred ms more, OK that's expected. How do you measure p50/p95?
04:29 Maya: Console exposes p50/p95/p99 per-route, per-model; you can also pull trace data via our API for fine-grained analysis.
04:38 Priya: Security \u0014 we need SSO, audit logs, and key rotation. Is that covered?
04:44 Javier: Yes, Hosted supports RBAC, enterprise SSO (SAML/SCIM), audit logs and integrates with customer KMS for dedicated/private plans. For Hosted API we store keys encrypted and rotate, and we provide detailed audit logs. We'll attach the security whitepaper.
05:02 Samantha: Any PII handling or redaction features?
05:07 Maya: We offer optional request/response redaction and configurable retention windows; for regulated flows many customers choose Private or Dedicated with customer-managed keys. We'll map the options in the security doc.
05:20 Marcus: Can you talk about retries and duplicate output when we retry on client timeout? We got duplicates with other providers.
05:28 Maya: By default if you retry the same request you may see duplicates unless you use idempotency tokens for non-streaming. For streaming use cases we recommend client-side resume or dedupe based on server-provided message ids. We'll share best-practice snippets.
05:47 Maya: Now switching to Console \u0014 showing routes, model pinned versions, token cost breakdown. You can set per-route defaults for temperature and max_tokens to avoid accidental cost spikes.
06:05 Marcus: Does Console let us see per-token cost by prompt?
06:10 Maya: Yes, per-call cost and token breakdowns are visible; we have filters for time range, route, and model. You can export to CSV.
06:18 Samantha: For the pilot, we plan to send production traffic for the checkout upsell flow. What would the on-ramp look like?
06:25 Javier: Typical on-ramp: 1) trial keys for benchmarking (we'll provide 30 days), 2) run your synthetic load, 3) Redwood provides a recommended model and batching settings, 4) optional canary routing in Console. For a production pilot we usually start with a few routes and monitor metrics for 1-2 weeks.
06:42 Priya: Who from Redwood will be our support contact during the pilot?
06:45 Javier: AE is primary contact; Maya will handle technical triage, and we provide onboarding sessions with Solutions if needed.
06:52 Marcus: Regarding model variants and fallbacks \u0014 if capacity drops do you automatically route to smaller models? We can't risk a complete outage.
06:59 Maya: Yes, smart routing policies can fallback to compatible variants by policy (latency first, cost first). You can configure automatic fallback to ensure availability with graceful degradation.
07:15 Samantha: Pricing \u0014 rough ballpark for 2M tokens/mo?
07:20 Javier: I'll send a tailored estimate, but expect discounts for committed reserved capacity; Hosted pay-as-you-go is straightforward and we'll present both.
07:28 Marcus: Thoughts on caching to reduce cost? We have many repeat prompts.
07:32 Maya: We support prefix/KV caching at the request layer; Console will show cache hit ratios and recommend cache TTLs. Caching can significantly reduce tokens for repeat prompts.
07:45 Priya: Any known gotchas with streaming and mobile clients?
07:50 Maya: Mobile can benefit from streaming for perceived latency, but keep in mind network jitter \u0014 implement reconnect/resume. SDKs have helpers.
07:58 Liam: Also note TLS, keep-alive, and efficient connection reuse help.
08:05 Samantha: Great. Can you summarize next steps?
08:10 Javier: Sure \u0014 we'll send pricing and pilot contract, Maya will send security docs and SOC2, Marcus will run benchmarks with trial keys, and we'll reconvene after results to discuss Dedicated/VPC if needed.
08:22 Priya: Perfect. Thank you.
08:25 Samantha: Thanks everyone.

(Transcript continues with some smaller clarifications, filler talk, and scheduling logistics)

10:12 Maya: Quick extra note \u0014 common retries pattern: set a short client timeout < server timeout, use idempotency token on create-style requests, and dedupe on server ids when possible. We'll email a snippet.
10:35 Marcus: Sounds good. One last asked: do you provide client SDKs for Node, Python, Go?
10:40 Liam: Yes, official SDKs for Python/Node/Go and a CLI. All include streaming helpers.
10:50 Samantha: Ok that's everything from my side.
10:55 Javier: Thanks again, we'll follow up with docs and the pricing sheet.
11:00 Meeting end
